answer:
Calculate the Taylor number for Taylor-Couette flow using the following parameters.
Inner cylinder radius R_in = 0.05 m.
Outer cylinder radius R_out = 0.052 m.
Radial gap Δr = 0.002 m.
Inner cylinder angular velocity ω_in = 2π × 100 / 60 rad/s (100 RPM).
Outer cylinder is stationary, ω_out = 0.
Dynamic viscosity μ = 0.01 Pa·s.
Assume fluid density ρ = 1000 kg/m³ (water) and compute kinematic viscosity ν = μ/ρ = 1×10⁻⁵ m²/s.
Use the Taylor number formula Ta = (R_in × (ω_in − ω_out) × Δr)² / (ν² × R_out).
State the water-density assumption explicitly in the working.
Report the final numerical value of Ta.
